- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward correction — price may rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike, forecast should not immediately continue rising — introduce a lagged mean-reversion bias.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 80+ day high), forecast should not persist above 10% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +/– 0.3), forecast should be less aggressive and include a smoothing factor.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >15% from forecast mean, check sentiment for “reversal” signals — adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average.
